name: My Stories
summary: Shopify app that adds Instagram-style video stories, shoppable clips and a lead form to product pages, with a free plan for 10 videos.
best_for: small Shopify stores with product videos that want Instagram-style stories, shoppable clips and a lead form without custom code
skip_if: your store is not on Shopify, you want more than 100 videos without paying $45 a month, or you want a tool we have tested ourselves
honest_knock: The free plan carries a watermark and stops at 10 videos. Lead capture is capped at 20 a month on the $14 plan, so a store that gets real traffic moves to $45 quickly. Plan names differ between the vendor site and the Shopify listing. We have not installed the app, so the lead sync and speed claims are the vendor's own.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on getmystories.com/pricing, US dollars) Beginner: $0, up to 10 uploaded videos, unlimited views, shoppable videos, watermark. Advanced: $14 a month, up to 100 videos, up to 20 leads a month, analytics, no watermark. Pro: $45 a month, unlimited videos and leads. 7-day free trial on paid plans. The Shopify listing shows yearly prices of $140 and $450. We have not installed the app.

schema_offer.description: Advanced, per month, 7-day free trial; Beginner free with watermark; Pro $45 per month. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

free_plan_evidence: (read 2026-11-17 on getmystories.com/pricing, US dollars) Beginner: $0, up to 10 uploaded videos, unlimited views, shoppable videos, watermark.

compare_with.name: Essential Cart Drawer
compare_with.why: Both are Shopify apps that change what shoppers see on the storefront, but My Stories is about video and lead capture while a cart drawer is about checkout. Compare which gap in your store is costing more.

purchase.how: AIBuilder Marketplace does not sell this software. Sign up, start a trial or buy on the vendor's site.
purchase.disclosure: Where purchase.affiliate is true, purchase.handoff_url is our own review page for the product; the vendor button on that page is a marked affiliate link and AIBuilder Marketplace may earn a commission at no extra cost to the buyer. Commission never changes what a record says, and products are not ranked by commission. Where it is false the link is the vendor's plain site. Since schema 1.1 this API does not publish affiliate links.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested My Stories on a Shopify development store. The core action, making a story from an uploaded video, did not succeed because our browser tool could not reach the upload button inside the iframe of the app; that is a limit of the test tool and not a finding about the app. Seen were the install permissions, the plan screen with Free, Pro and Advanced, the Shopify approval screen for Pro (not approved), the Lead Form page on the Free plan, the upload screen, the Link Video page and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English, https://apps.shopify.com/videos-stories-on-products) opened the Install app dialog in the admin, which asked for View customer data (Sensitive data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, Online Store, Shopify admin). The install was started at about 14:57 and approved at about 14:58, and about 1 minute after the start the app showed the screen Select a plan (/app/pricing); there was no other onboarding. Core action NOT DONE: the goal was to upload a video, link it to a test product and show it in the theme preview. This did not succeed. The reason was our browser tool and not the app: the app runs in a cross-origin iframe, and with our browser tools the file input of the upload button could not be reached, so the system file picker could not be used. A test video of 4 seconds (540x960, no faces) was ready but could not be offered to the app. The app was therefore not tried on its core action, and nothing here is a finding against the app. No story was made, no preview was seen, no theme change was made and nothing was saved in the theme. What was seen: the start screen Welcome to My Stories (You can upload vertical Story videos and display them on your product pages, collections, standalone pages, or homepage.) with 1 out of 6 steps completed (Upload your first video, Link your video to a product, Add Stories block to product page / collections page / Homepage / page template); the empty video library (No videos uploaded yet.); the Upload Video screen (Start uploading videos, with the button Upload Videos); and the Link Video page with four choices, Link to products, Link to collections, Link to homepage and Link to pages. Up to this point the steps were: install (2 clicks), choose a plan (1 click) and go to the upload screen (2 clicks). Plans: the in-app screen, the same as the App Store, has a switch Pay monthly or Pay yearly. Free: Up to 10 videos uploaded, Unlimited videos views, Link videos everywhere, Shoppables Videos, Watermark. Pro: $14.00 a month, 7 trial days, Everything in Free, Up to 100 videos uploaded, Lead Form, Up to 20 leads per month, Story performance analytics, NO watermark. Advanced: $45.00 a month, 7 trial days, Everything in Pro, Unlimited uploaded videos, Lead Form, Unlimited leads per month, Story performance analytics, NO watermark. The App Store lists $140 a year and $450 a year and a 7-day free trial. Deviation from the dossier: the dossier names the plans Beginner at $0, Advanced at $14 and Pro at $45, while the app and the App Store call them Free, Pro at $14 and Advanced at $45, so the names of the two paid plans are swapped. Checkout: the Free plan was chosen first (no approval screen; the button became Current plan). Then Pro was clicked to see the checkout: the Shopify Approve subscription screen shows My Stories by GetMyStories, plan Pro, $14,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a subtotal of $14,00 plus any applicable taxes, a total of $14,00 due 24 Nov., an Add payment method row and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen and a payment method was asked, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. The Cancel button gave a toast: The shop cannot accept the provided charge. Advanced was not opened. Lead Form: on the Free plan the page says Available on paid plans (The lead form and leads list are available on Advanced and Pro plans), and the switch Enable Lead Form is switched off and greyed out. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall) and the dialog Uninstall My Stories?, which says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Select all that apply); we gave Testing multiple apps at about 15:04 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: uploading a video, linking it to a product, the Stories block in the theme, the preview, the shoppable button, the Lead Form itself (it needs a paid plan), the analytics, the watermark, the loading speed and the paid plans. Clean up: nothing was created in the store and nothing was saved in the theme; the app was uninstalled; the test video stayed on our own side; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The plan screen comes straight after the install, before any onboarding; the Pro approval screen asks for a payment method and has no test charge sentence; its Cancel button gave a toast, The shop cannot accept the provided charge.; and the Lead Form page shows the whole form on the Free plan with the switch greyed out. The plan names in the dossier are swapped against the app.
